question: Vempati Chinna Satyam was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 1998. He was a _______ dancer.
solution:
The correct answer is Kuchipudi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vempati Chinna Satyam, who lived from 15 October 1929 to 29 July 2012, was a legend in the Kuchipudi dancing style.**
 
• He is credited with spreading the dancing style's popularity all over the world.
 
• He has received numerous honours, including the **Raja Lakshmi Award from Madras and the Sangeet Peeth of Bombay.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Kathak Dance**

 
 
• **One of the primary categories of ancient Indian classical dance, known as Kathak**, is thought to have started with the **wandering storytellers known as Kathakars in North India.**
 
• Similar to the early Greek theatre, these wandering **Kathakars **used music, dance, and songs to convey legendary tales.
 
• The** Bhakti movement**, a tendency of theistic devotion that emerged in **mediaeval Hinduism,** is when the genre first came into being.
 
 
 
• **Manipuri Dance**
 
 
• **Manipuri dance is one of India's most well-known classical dance** genres and is particularly renowned for its Vaishnavist themes and spectacular performances of **dance dramas centred on the love between Radha and Krishna known as "Ras Lila."**
 
• Additional subjects in this kind of art related to **Shaktism, Shaivism**, and the **sylvan gods known as Umang Lai during the Manipuri festival "Lai Haraoba."**
 
• Although this dance style has its roots in the **ancient Sanskrit Hindu literature "Natya Shastra," **it is named after the north-eastern Indian state of Manipur, where it first appeared.
 
 
 
• **Kathakali Dance**
 
 
• **An essential subgenre of Indian classical dance known as "Kathakali" **is linked to this **kind of storytelling.**
 
• It is a dance drama from Kerala in southern India. Like other **Indian traditional dance forms, "Kathakali"** uses spectacular facial and hand movements along with music and vocal performance to effectively convey the story to the audience.
